title: Sherman Institute at Riverside, where he started jazz trombone
summary: He applied to Sherman Institute in California after his stepfather died, played jazz in the dormitory, and had no particular trombone models.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: What kinds of music -- you were able to a, get into the concert band that they had, or was it a marching band that they had? What kinds of musical aggregations a, did they have that you performed in actually, once you started getting the trombone down?

Well, I didn't, perform any, any -- I wasn't good enough. I was good enough to be in the orchestra in the high school, but I didn't get to playing jazz until I -- that year, 1930. it was the year 1930 when my step-father died, and I said I might as well go to the Indian school. And that'd be one, one mouth less to feed because I always did eat, you know. I didn't . . . Anyway, I applied to Sherman Institute at Riverside, California, and they accepted me. Phoenix was full. I couldn't get to Phoenix, so this time I went to Sherman Institute at Riverside. And that's where I started the jazz trombone. And I would play jazz in my dormitory, and all the kids would be listening there. Then they're egging me on, 'Play more; play more.'

Who were, at the time -- Louis certainly inspired you musically, but were there any trombonists that you were aware of, through recordings or what have you, that you liked, and that also inspired you?
I'm sorry to say I didn't have any, any -- I didn't follow anybody because I was too busy going to school. But I, learned there how to play jazz.
